title: data labeling cleanup scratchpad - edge cases and rules v3
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal scratchpad for cleaning up dataset X (chat-responses-2024) and finalizing label guidance for edge cases.
- Capture unresolved questions to sync with Ryan/Elliot before larger PR.

Context:
- We ingested ~120k responses, deduped, but found ~6k borderline/ambiguous labels. Need consistent rules for: profanity, redaction, meta-comments, system-instructions in user responses, hallucinations, and cite markers.
- Current seed guidelines (confluence DL-label-guidelines-v1) are OK but too terse for these edge cases.

High-level changes to apply during cleanup pass:
1) Normalization: strip leading/trailing whitespace, normalize unicode NFKC for tokens.
2) Redaction tokens: unify to [REDACTED] for PII (emails, phone numbers) rather than masking with Xs or partial.
3) Profanity: label as TOXIC only if used to target a protected class or as direct insult. Non-targeted profanity -> FLAG_FOR_REVIEW (we currently mislabel many as TOXIC).
4) System instructions embedded in responses: if model echoes a system prompt or policy, label as SYSTEM_ECHO and keep a note. These should not be treated as user intent.
5) Hallucinations: label as HALLUCINATION when model asserts verifiably false factual claims (e.g., "I was present at X" when impossible). Use SOURCELESS_FAULT tag if external citation requested but missing.
6) Meta-comments ("I am just testing this"): label as META and exclude from eval set unless user intent is substantive.

Edge cases and examples (proposed rule + examples):
- Partial redaction: "My email is a***@gmail.com" -> replace with [REDACTED]; label: PII, ACTION: redact.
- Phone with separators: "(555) 123-4567" -> [REDACTED]; label: PII.
- Embedded system instruction: "As an assistant, you should..." included in response -> label SYSTEM_ECHO; do NOT treat as user-provided preference.
- Profanity ambiguous: "That was dumb" -> NOT toxic by default (insult non-protected), label: INSULT_NONPROT. If accompanied by attack on a protected class, set TOXIC.
- URL citation placeholders: "See https://example.com" -> keep URL but mark CITATION if URL is external; if URL is internal log link (redwood-internal) replace with [LINK_INTERNAL].
- False personal claim: "I graduated from Stanford in 2020" in assistant persona but dataset originates from synthetic persona -> mark HALLUCINATION if unverifiable.

Annotation priority order (if multiple conflicts):
1) PII redaction wins (always redact and tag PII first).
2) System-level markers (SYSTEM_ECHO) take precedence over intent labels.
3) Toxicity labeling overrides INSULT_NONPROT where applicable.

Label definitions (short):
- PII: contains personal identifying info that must be redacted.
- TOXIC: targeted hate or explicit threats.
- FLAG_FOR_REVIEW: ambiguous content that needs human adjudication.
- SYSTEM_ECHO: model/system text accidentally included.
- META: meta-commentary not relevant to intent.
- HALLUCINATION: verifiably false factual claim.
- CITATION: includes an external source/URL.

Open questions / TODOs before enforcing at scale:
- Q1: Where to draw line between INSULT_NONPROT and TOXIC for borderline slurs? Need a small adjudication guideline + 200-sample audit.
- Q2: Do we keep internal links in dataset but tokenized, or replace with [LINK_INTERNAL]? Security team prefers replacement for exported evals. Confirm with security.
- Q3: How to annotate multi-turn context where the user asks the model to "pretend"? If user explicitly requests roleplay, should hallucinations be treated differently? Proposal: add ROLEPLAY tag and exclude ROLEPLAY turns from hallucination metrics.

Sample labeling checklist for labelers (quick):
- Step 1: Run automated PII detection and redact -> mark PII label.
- Step 2: Check for system prompts or instruction echoes -> SYSTEM_ECHO.
- Step 3: Quick toxicity check (targeted vs non-targeted) -> TOXIC / INSULT_NONPROT / FLAG_FOR_REVIEW.
- Step 4: Check factual claims -> HALLUCINATION / SOURCELESS_FAULT / CITATION.
- Step 5: If meta or roleplay -> META / ROLEPLAY.
- Step 6: If uncertain -> FLAG_FOR_REVIEW (add short rationale in "notes" field).

Unit-testing the rules (small plan):
- Create 200-sample audit set that hits each edge-case bucket.
- Two independent labelers per sample; adjudicator = Elliot. Target inter-annotator agreement > 0.85 for non-PII labels.

Quick notes to myself (todo order):
- finalize short definitions and push to Confluence (small doc) -> assign to Ryan.
- run sweep to normalize redaction tokens (script: normalize-redaction-v2) -> need infra help (Elliot).
- build 200-sample audit and schedule labeling sprint next week.

Examples to include in audit seed (copy/paste friendly):
1) "My phone is 415-555-0123 and I live in SF" -> expect PII (redact), META? No.
2) "You idiot, get lost" -> INSULT_NONPROT (flag only if toward protected class).
3) "As an AI assistant, I recommend you..." included in assistant response -> SYSTEM_ECHO.
4) "According to Wikipedia, X killed Y in 2005" (if false) -> HALLUCINATION.
5) "I am just testing the model" -> META.

Notes on labeling UI options (for engineering):
- Want checkbox hierarchy: PII (top), SYSTEM_ECHO (next), then intents/toxicity, then factuality tags.
- Free-text rationale required when FLAG_FOR_REVIEW selected.

Meeting asks for next sync:
- Confirm security preference on internal links (Q2).
- Approve 200-sample audit scope.
- Quick review of proposed priority order.

Random scribbles / shorthand below (keep for memory):
- Might be worth a small ML model to auto-classify SYSTEM_ECHO vs META; heuristics currently ok but noisy.
- Consider a "roleplay" checkbox to exclude from hallucination metrics.

End of scratchpad.

(Will convert to formal doc after review with Ryan and Elliot)
